p: "Fortunate is the people that knows the teruah"
וְכִי אֵין אֻמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם יוֹדְעִין לְהָרִיעַ?
"Do the nations of the world not know how to sound a teruah?
How many trumpets they have! etc.
Rather, it means that they know how
to win over their Creator with the teruah."
"Fortunate is the portion of the tzaddikim
who know how to direct their will
and who know how to rectify the world
on this day with the sound of the shofar;
and of this it is written,
'Fortunate is the people that knows the teruah' —
That is, the main intent of the blasts
is to fulfill the command of the Creator,
and to hear the sound of the shofar,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מְתַקְּנִים כָּל הָעוֹלָם,
and through this they rectify the whole world,
as it says, "to rectify the world."
And this is the meaning of "that knows the teruah":
to bring da'as into the heart;
"Da'as — this is one who recognizes his Creator."
His statutes and His judgments to Yisrael," etc.,
"His words," which are the words of Torah,
"a heritage of the congregation of Yaakov,"
and a gentile who engages in Torah is liable to death
for the nations of the world were commanded
and they are not permitted to add
any mitzvah of their own accord;
or he remains with his own law
פֶּרֶק י מֵהִלְכוֹת מְלָכִים, הֲלָכָה ט).
Therefore the people of Shechem became liable to death,
because they added the mitzvah of milah
not for the sake of conversion.
which are mitzvos that reason obligates —
they are permitted, and it is fitting for them,
to conduct themselves by them as a matter of derech eretz,
on account of the honoring of his father that he had fulfilled,
he has been sitting and honoring his parents," etc.,
even though Eisav had uprooted the name of Yisrael
and was like a Ben Noach.
"'The kindness of the nations is sin' —
all kindness that the nations do
since they do it only to aggrandize themselves, etc.;
only so that their kingdom will endure;
they do it only to show off."
In this, the sin is only
when their intent is not for the sake of Heaven;
even though these are not among the seven mitzvos.
That is because honoring parents and tzedakah
are among the mitzvos that reason obligates,
and they may fulfill them on account of reason
But of them it is said,
for with them, the judgments they do
do not bring da'as into their hearts,
the da'as of one who recognizes his Creator,
for them, the judgments too bring
da'as and recognition of the Creator into the heart.
And this is what is said,
"Fortunate is the people that knows the teruah":
the teruah brings da'as into their hearts,
for they intend to do the will of their Master,
and by this they rectify the whole world;
and "they know how to win over their Creator with the teruah."
And it all has one intent:
that through the mitzvos they recognize the Creator,
and it brings da'as into their hearts.
